rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window and critical pairs while minimizing the risk of missing strongly retained compounds. A midrange temperature leaves room to probe temperature-dependent selectivity in either direction.

Change only gradient duration to determine whether the tightly clustered early peaks respond to slope. This also tests whether the later marginal pair gains resolution before refining the solvent window or temperature.

Test a substantial temperature increase at the original gradient slope to shift selectivity within the early three-peak cluster. Higher temperature should also shorten retention, preserving room for a shallower gradient if needed.
The temperature increase resolved most of the early cluster, leaving only one pair at R = 1.14. A shallower gradient may bring that pair above 1.5 while keeping the last peak within 10 minutes.

The remaining close pair did not improve with a shallower gradient, so test a higher starting organic fraction to shift its selectivity. Keep temperature at 60 C and duration at 10 minutes, where retention remains comfortably below the time penalty threshold.

Increase the starting organic fraction another step to exploit the improvement in the remaining critical pair. The first peak should still be retained, and the other pairs currently have resolution margin.

The maximum CRF has been reached; now shorten the gradient by one step to seek a faster fully resolved method. Keep the solvent endpoints and temperature fixed to measure the resolution cost of compression.

Narrow the gradient window to restore resolution to the two pairs just below 1.5 at eight minutes. This intermediate slope should retain much of the speed gain, with the final organic fraction still comfortably above the last peak’s estimated elution composition.

Test one higher starting-organic step to shorten retention and potentially strengthen the limiting pair. Monitor the early peaks closely, since reduced initial retention could compromise their separation; injection 8 remains the faster fully resolved fallback.

Lower temperature one step to test whether increased early retention can recover the limiting pair at the higher starting organic fraction. This probes a possible faster fully resolved alternative while retaining injection 8 as the established fallback.

Probe the low-temperature selectivity regime, where the early cluster may reorder and separate differently from the high-temperature optimum. The steep gradient and strong endpoint limit the retention-time increase; injection 8 remains the fully resolved fallback.

Return to the successful high-temperature window and trim the endpoint to just above the last peak’s estimated elution composition. This six-minute gradient is slightly shallower than injection 8, aiming to preserve full resolution with a shorter programmed gradient.

Increase the endpoint one step to test a slope between the fastest fully resolved method and the slightly under-resolved eight-minute run. This targets a last peak below six minutes while checking whether the limiting pair retains R ≥ 1.5.

Injection 13 is marginally under-resolved despite its rounded CRF, so retain injection 8 as the fastest confirmed fully resolved method. Test a shallower gradient at phi0 = 0.20 to recover the early limiting pair and seek greater resolution margin while remaining below ten minutes.

The higher starting fraction requires a substantially shallower gradient, so return to phi0 = 0.15 and test a moderate slope for greater resolution margin. This should remain below the ten-minute time threshold while providing a less marginal maximum-score alternative.

Preserve injection 8’s initial gradient slope but end the ramp earlier, testing whether a shorter program can retain maximum CRF. The late compounds will likely elute during the hold, so their retention times and resolution will determine whether this endpoint is sufficient.

Ending the gradient early delayed the last peak, so retain injection 8 as the fastest confirmed fully resolved method. Test a modestly shallower slope to increase the limiting pair’s resolution margin while keeping all peaks within ten minutes.

Return toward the fastest fully resolved method, lowering its endpoint one grid step to give the limiting pair slightly more resolution margin. This should preserve maximum CRF with a last peak around 6.4 minutes, substantially faster than injection 17.

Refine the fully resolved higher-starting-organic method from injection 14 by shortening its gradient and trimming the endpoint. The nearly unchanged slope should preserve resolution while modestly shortening retention; injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Trim injection 15’s solvent window and programmed duration while retaining a similar slope, targeting its greater resolution margin without a time penalty. The endpoint remains above the estimated last-peak elution composition; injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Shorten injection 20’s programmed gradient and trim its endpoint, using a slightly steeper slope that should still fully resolve the early cluster. Check whether the last peak clears promptly near the gradient end; injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved fallback.

Test the next faster grid neighbor of injection 8 to establish the speed boundary directly. The limiting pair may fall just below 1.5; if so, injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method.

Back off the under-resolved eight-minute gradient by one duration step, targeting full resolution with modest margin and no time penalty. Injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method; this tests a nearby, less marginal alternative.

Combine injection 23’s successful gradient slope with a shorter programmed duration and lower endpoint, which should still exceed the last peak’s elution composition. This targets full resolution with modest margin; injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed maximum-score method.

Use the final injection to test a maximum-score alternative between injections 15 and 17, targeting a minimum resolution near 1.6 with the last peak below eight minutes. Injection 8 remains the fastest confirmed fully resolved method, and the campaign has already reached the maximum CRF.
